text:
Michael DiPietro stopped all 28 shots he saw, and Boston turned that shutout into a 6-0 rout of Nashville at TD Garden. DiPietro's night was better than the clean sheet suggests. By expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the raw count of shots, Nashville generated 3.38 of them, and DiPietro saved 3.38 goals more than an average goalie would have allowed on those shots. Justus Annunen, at the other end, faced 31 shots and let in six.

The game was not as lopsided as the score. Nashville actually had more shot attempts, 61 to 57, and in the third period the Predators held a slight edge in chance quality, 1.54 to 1.38 in expected goals. But Boston won the quality battle overall, 4.48 to 3.38, and by the measure of simulated replays of every shot, the Bruins deserved to win 67 percent of the time. Boston owned the second period, 1.94 to 1.20, and pulled away there with goals from David Pastrnak and JJ Peterka. Peterka's was the one real gift, a chance that scored 73 percent of the time. Most of the others were modest looks that went in anyway.

Pastrnak finished with two goals and two assists, and Charlie McAvoy had four assists without a goal. Casey Mittelstadt, Elias Lindholm (on the power play) and Mark Kastelic also scored. Boston went 1 for 3 with the man advantage, and Nashville was 0 for 1. The facts here don't include standings or streaks, so the result stands on its own: a shutout for Boston's goalie, and a night Annunen and Nashville will want to put behind them.
